content: The provided text is a detailed description of drug interactions involving elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF (commonly used in HIV treatment regimens). 1. Phenytoin: Phenytoin reduces the levels of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Conversely, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF decreases phenytoin levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 2. Pimavanserin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pimavanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 3. Pimozide: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pimozide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening events. 4. Pindolol: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pindolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Piroxicam: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Avoid combining emtricitabine and tenofovir with high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs due to potential nephrotoxicity. 6. Pirtobrutinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the dose is already 50 mg/day, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. 7. Polatuzumab Vedotin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases polatuzumab vedotin toxicity by increasing unconjugated MMAE (a CYP3A4 substrate). Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Polymyxin B: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Pomalidomide: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pomalidomide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Ponatinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg/day. 11. Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Pralsetinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Praziquantel: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Primidone: Primidone decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to virologic failure and resistance. 15. Procainamide: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases procainamide levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 16. Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, or Natural): Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 17. Promethazine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases promethazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Propofol: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF decreases propofol levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Propranolol: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases propranolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 20. Protriptyline: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases protriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 21. Quazepam: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases quazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing benzodiazepine doses. 22. Quetiapine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. If necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose. 23. Quinidine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 24. Quinine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Quizartinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the quizartinib dose or discontinue during inhibitor use. 26. Rabeprazole: No clinically significant interactions are expected between elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and rabeprazole based on drug interaction studies. 27. Raltgravir: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete HIV regimen and should not be coadministered with other antiretrovirals, including raltegravir. 28. Ranolazine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Regorafenib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is contraindicated with regorafenib due to CYP3A4 inhibition, which increases regorafenib levels and decreases exposure to its active metabolites. 30. Repaglinide: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases repaglinide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Repotrectinib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Discontinue CYP3A inhibitors before initiating repotrectinib. 32. Resmetirom: Avoid coadministration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 33. Ribociclib: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ribociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the ribociclib dose to 400 mg/day. 34. Rifabutin: Rifabutin decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Conversely, elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases rifabutin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 35. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to virologic failure and resistance. 36. Rifapentine: Rifapentine decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 37. Rifaximin: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases rifaximin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Rilpivirine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete HIV regimen and should not be coadministered with other antiretrovirals, including rilpivirine. 39. Rimegepant: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Riociguat: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases riociguat levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for hypotension and adjust the dose as needed. 41. Risperidone: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases risperidone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A dose reduction of risperidone may be required. 42. Ritonavir: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete HIV regimen and should not be coadministered with other antiretrovirals, including ritonavir.
